End of claims-based follow-up

Source: R/claims_followup_end.R
claims_followup_end.Rd

For each row, finds the last day of follow-up for a claims-based outcome: the earliest of death, the end of the Medicare-primary coverage spell containing the index date, the date the claims are complete to, a study end date, and a maximum length of follow-up. Every end date is the last day observed, so a patient is followed from index_date through followup_end, both included.

Usage

claims_followup_end(
  df,
  index_date,
  coverage_end,
  death_date = NULL,
  claims_end,
  study_end = NULL,
  max_days = NULL
)

Arguments

df

A data frame with a column USRDS_ID and the columns named below.

index_date

The name of a Date column in df: the first day of follow-up. A missing value means follow-up never starts: followup_end is then NA, with reason "no_index".

coverage_end

The name of a Date column in df holding the end of the Medicare-primary spell that contains the index date, as returned by verify_medicare_primary() through coverage_end_variable. A missing value means the patient has no Medicare-primary spell at the index date: followup_end is then NA, with reason "no_coverage".

death_date

Optional name of a Date column in df holding the date of death (for example DIED from the patients file). A missing value means the patient is not known to have died.

claims_end

Required. The last date the claims are complete to, for the release in use (as.Date("2023-12-31") for the 2025 standard analysis files). It has no default because it changes with every release.

study_end

Optional last day of the study: a Date, or the name of a Date column in df.

max_days

Optional largest number of whole days after the index date; the last day is index_date + max_days.

Value

df with two added columns: followup_end (Date) and followup_end_reason, one of "death", "coverage_end", "claims_end", "study_end", "max_days", "no_coverage" or "no_index". When two ends fall on the same day, the reason is the first in that order. A missing index date takes precedence over missing coverage.

Details

Claims end before the payer history and the death records do: in the 2025 standard analysis files, claims are complete through 2023-12-31 while the core files run through 2024-12-31 (Researcher's Guide 2025, Section 5, "Introduction"). An open payer spell is given the end of the data period as its ENDDATE (Section 4, "ESRD Payer Sequence File"), so the coverage end alone does not stop follow-up when the claims stop. The 2017 Annual Data Report (Volume 2, ESRD Analytical Methods, hospitalization) censors at death, at the end of Medicare Parts A and B or Medicare primary, and at December 31.

Examples

patients <- data.frame(
  USRDS_ID = c(1, 2),
  index = as.Date(c("2015-01-01", "2015-01-01")),
  DIED = as.Date(c("2015-03-01", NA)),
  coverage_end = as.Date(c("2016-12-31", "2015-06-30"))
)
claims_followup_end(
  patients,
  index_date = "index",
  coverage_end = "coverage_end",
  death_date = "DIED",
  claims_end = as.Date("2023-12-31"),
  max_days = 364
)
#>   USRDS_ID      index       DIED coverage_end followup_end followup_end_reason
#> 1        1 2015-01-01 2015-03-01   2016-12-31   2015-03-01               death
#> 2        2 2015-01-01       <NA>   2015-06-30   2015-06-30        coverage_end
